Pattern: Universal Forwarder file monitoring — Splunk Cloud
Source data: Host operating-system, application, security, audit and custom file-based logs, including Windows Event Logs and Linux/Unix logs.
Required app / add-on: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux or vendor TA
Port / firewall requirements: Allow outbound TCP 9997 to <stack>.splunkcloud.com; allow outbound TCP 8089 to the deployment server where the forwarder or Heavy Forwarder is centrally managed. Permit DNS resolution and TLS certificate validation paths.
Authentication requirements: The forwarder service account requires read access to the selected files or Windows channels. Splunk forwarding uses the configured TLS certificate or mutual-TLS trust; no source API key is required.
Source platform requirements: Define monitored file paths or Windows channels, file ownership and permissions, log rotation behaviour, hostname handling, index, sourcetype and expected event volume. Record the deployment server and receiving target.

Authentication requirements: The forwarder service account requires read access to the selected files or Windows channels. Splunk forwarding uses the configured TLS certificate or mutual-TLS trust; no source API key is required.
Source platform requirements: Define monitored file paths or Windows channels, file ownership and permissions, log rotation behaviour, hostname handling, index, sourcetype and expected event volume. Record the deployment server and receiving target.

Pattern: Syslog via SC4S — Splunk Cloud
Source data: Network and security appliance syslog, such as firewall, router, switch, VPN, proxy, load balancer and infrastructure events.
Port / firewall requirements: Allow source devices to SC4S on UDP/TCP 514 or TCP 6514 for TLS, as selected; allow TCP 443 from SC4S to Splunk Cloud HEC. Restrict listeners to approved source networks.
Authentication requirements: UDP/TCP syslog normally has no application credential. For TLS syslog, configure server certificates and optionally mutual TLS. SC4S requires a dedicated Splunk HEC token for onward delivery.
Source platform requirements: Record each device or platform hostname/IP, vendor and product, destination SC4S address, protocol and port, facility/severity, message template, timezone and expected EPS. Configure the matching SC4S vendor source and metadata rules.

Source platform requirements: Record each device or platform hostname/IP, vendor and product, destination SC4S address, protocol and port, facility/severity, message template, timezone and expected EPS. Configure the matching SC4S vendor source and metadata rules.

Pattern: HTTP Event Collector — Splunk Cloud
Source data: Application, service and integration events or metrics formatted as HEC event or raw payloads.
Port / firewall requirements: Allow source systems to TCP 443 to the Splunk Cloud HEC endpoint. Permit DNS resolution and TLS certificate validation; restrict access to approved source networks or egress addresses.
Authentication requirements: Use a dedicated HTTP Event Collector token with least-privilege index access. Validate the server certificate; use client certificates or mutual TLS only where the published endpoint requires it.
Source platform requirements: Provide the HEC endpoint, token reference, event or raw endpoint, target index, sourcetype, source and host values, payload schema, timestamp format, batching limits and whether indexer acknowledgement is required.

Pattern: REST API or modular input — Splunk Cloud
Source data: Vendor platform or SaaS audit, activity, alert, inventory, configuration and operational records exposed by REST API.
Port / firewall requirements: Allow outbound TCP 443 from the Heavy Forwarder or IDM to the vendor API; allow outbound TCP 9997 to <stack>.splunkcloud.com; allow outbound TCP 8089 to the deployment server where the forwarder or Heavy Forwarder is centrally managed. Add proxy or private-endpoint rules where required.
Authentication requirements: Configure the vendor-supported credential, such as OAuth 2.0 client credentials, API key, bearer token, certificate or service username/password. Store secrets in the add-on credential store and grant only the API scopes required for the selected datasets.
Source platform requirements: Provide the API base URL and region, tenant/account/organisation identifier where applicable, enabled API datasets, endpoint paths, polling interval, lookback window, pagination or cursor method, rate limits, checkpoint location and expected volume.

Pattern: Azure Event Hub — Splunk Cloud
Source data: Azure activity, Entra ID, resource diagnostic, security, platform and application logs or metrics streamed through Event Hub.
Required app / add-on: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services
Port / firewall requirements: Allow outbound TCP 5671 for AMQP over TLS and/or TCP 443 for HTTPS or AMQP-over-WebSockets to <eventhub-namespace>.servicebus.windows.net. If the input runs on an IDM or Heavy Forwarder, also allow outbound TCP 9997 to <stack>.splunkcloud.com. Allow Azure identity endpoints over TCP 443 when using Microsoft Entra authentication.
Authentication requirements: Use either a least-privilege Event Hubs shared access policy/connection string with Listen permission, or a Microsoft Entra application or managed identity with the required Event Hubs data receiver role. Record tenant ID, client ID and secret/certificate reference when service-principal authentication is used.
Source platform requirements: Provide Azure tenant ID, subscription ID, resource group, Event Hub namespace, Event Hub name, consumer group, authentication entity or policy name, diagnostic setting name, enabled log categories, partition count and retention. Ensure only one active consumer uses the designated consumer group unless the design supports sharing.

Pattern: AWS S3 and SQS — Splunk Cloud
Source data: AWS service logs stored in S3, such as CloudTrail, VPC Flow, ELB/ALB, CloudFront, WAF and access logs.
Port / firewall requirements: Allow outbound TCP 443 to the required AWS regional endpoints for S3, SQS, STS and KMS where encryption is used. If collection runs on a Heavy Forwarder, also allow outbound TCP 9997 to <stack>.splunkcloud.com and outbound TCP 8089 to the deployment server where the forwarder or Heavy Forwarder is centrally managed. PrivateLink endpoints may replace internet egress where approved.
Authentication requirements: Prefer an IAM role or STS AssumeRole trust. Where access keys are unavoidable, store the access key ID and secret securely and rotate them. Grant only required S3 Get/List, SQS Receive/Delete/GetQueueAttributes and KMS Decrypt permissions.
Source platform requirements: Provide AWS account ID, region, S3 bucket and prefix, SQS queue URL/ARN, notification configuration, role ARN and external ID where used, KMS key ARN for SSE-KMS, log file format/compression and expected delivery delay and volume.

Pattern: DB Connect — Splunk Cloud
Source data: Relational database records returned by SQL queries, including audit, transaction, reference and operational tables.
Port / firewall requirements: Allow the DB Connect host to the database listener on the database-specific port, such as TCP 1433 for SQL Server, 1521 for Oracle, 5432 for PostgreSQL or 3306 for MySQL; allow outbound TCP 9997 to <stack>.splunkcloud.com where DB Connect is on a separate collection tier; allow outbound TCP 8089 to the deployment server where the forwarder or Heavy Forwarder is centrally managed.
Authentication requirements: Use a dedicated least-privilege database account, integrated/Kerberos identity, wallet or client certificate as supported. Grant read/execute rights only to the required schemas, views, tables or stored procedures and protect the credential in DB Connect.
Source platform requirements: Provide database host/FQDN, listener port, database or service name, JDBC driver and URL, schema, table/query or stored procedure, rising/checkpoint column, timestamp and timezone handling, batch size, polling schedule and expected row volume.

Pattern: Federated Search to S3 — Splunk Cloud
Source data: Archived or historical structured datasets in Amazon S3, catalogued for search-time access.
Port / firewall requirements: Allow outbound TCP 443 from the federated search or search tier to the required AWS S3, STS, Glue Data Catalog and KMS regional endpoints. Use approved proxy or private endpoints where required.
Authentication requirements: Use a least-privilege IAM role or STS AssumeRole configuration. Grant the required S3 read/list, Glue catalog read and KMS decrypt permissions; use an external ID for cross-account trust where applicable.
Source platform requirements: Provide AWS account ID, region, S3 bucket and prefix, file format and compression, partition layout, Glue Data Catalog database and table, role ARN, external ID, KMS key ARN, data retention and expected search concurrency.

Pattern: Edge or Ingest Processor routing — Splunk Cloud
Source data: Any upstream structured or unstructured telemetry requiring filtering, masking, enrichment, sourcetype assignment or destination routing.
Port / firewall requirements: Allow the source-specific inbound or outbound collection protocol and allow TCP 443 to the Splunk Cloud ingest or HEC endpoint. Allow TCP 443 to the processor management plane and certificate/identity endpoints where required.
Authentication requirements: Authentication depends on the selected input. Use HEC tokens, OAuth credentials, API keys, certificates or mutual TLS as required by the source, and a dedicated destination token or output credential for the Splunk destination.
Source platform requirements: Provide input endpoint and protocol, processor or tenant identifier, pipeline name/version, source schema, routing and masking rules, target index and sourcetype, output destination, certificate trust, failure route and expected throughput.

Source mechanism: Vendor cloud service API or supported cloud input
Port / firewall requirements: Allow TCP 443 between the Splunk Cloud input service and the vendor API or supported cloud endpoint. Where the vendor enforces network restrictions, configure approved IP allowlisting, private connectivity or service-specific firewall rules.

Pattern: On-premises app/add-on forwarding to Splunk Cloud — Splunk Cloud

Collection tier / runtime: On-premises Splunk Heavy Forwarder or IDM
Transport: Vendor-supported protocol, commonly HTTPS; Splunk-to-Splunk over TLS
Port / firewall requirements: Allow outbound TCP 443 or the vendor-specific protocol from the Heavy Forwarder/IDM to the source platform; allow outbound TCP 9997 to <stack>.splunkcloud.com; allow outbound TCP 8089 to the deployment server where the forwarder or Heavy Forwarder is centrally managed. Add proxy, private endpoint or security-zone rules as needed.
Authentication requirements: Use the credential supported by the on-premises add-on, such as OAuth client credentials, API key/token, certificate or service username/password. Store secrets on the approved Heavy Forwarder/IDM and use Splunk TLS trust for onward forwarding.

Confirm the add-on is supported on the selected Heavy Forwarder/IDM operating system.

Pattern: Splunk Stream network traffic collection — Splunk Cloud
Source data: Network packets, flows, protocol metadata, transactions and application-layer session data such as DNS, HTTP, TLS, TCP and UDP.
Source mechanism: Packet capture, mirrored traffic, TAP, SPAN or supported capture interface
Collection tier / runtime: Splunk Stream Forwarder or supported Stream capture component
Transport: Splunk-to-Splunk over TLS or supported Splunk forwarding path
Required app / add-on: Splunk App for Stream and associated Stream components
Port / firewall requirements: No source application port is required for passive TAP/SPAN capture. Allow outbound TCP 9997 to <stack>.splunkcloud.com from the Stream forwarder or capture tier and allow outbound TCP 8089 to the deployment server where the forwarder or Heavy Forwarder is centrally managed. Permit any Stream management communications required by the deployed topology.
Authentication requirements: Passive capture does not require a source API credential. The capture service requires operating-system packet-capture privileges, and Splunk forwarding/management uses the configured TLS certificates and platform credentials.
Source platform requirements: Provide TAP/SPAN source and destination configuration, capture interface/NIC, VLANs and network segments, link speed, packet truncation policy, BPF or protocol filters, promiscuous-mode approval, time synchronisation, Stream configuration and expected packet rate.

Pattern: Heavy Forwarder intermediary — Splunk Cloud
Source data: Any source telemetry that must traverse an approved intermediary, including syslog, API records, database rows, files, HEC payloads and forwarded events.
Source mechanism: Syslog, API, database, file, HEC or other supported input
Transport: Vendor-supported protocol such as syslog, HTTPS, JDBC, file monitoring or HEC; Splunk-to-Splunk over TLS
Required app / add-on: Install on the Heavy Forwarder when the app/add-on cannot run in Splunk Cloud
Port / firewall requirements: Allow only the source-specific protocol from the source security zone to the approved Heavy Forwarder; allow outbound TCP 9997 to <stack>.splunkcloud.com from the Heavy Forwarder to the final destination; allow outbound TCP 8089 to the deployment server where the forwarder or Heavy Forwarder is centrally managed. Document each firewall hop and asymmetric routing or proxy dependency.
Authentication requirements: Use the source-supported credential on the Heavy Forwarder, such as OAuth, API key, service account, certificate, database account or HEC token. Use dedicated Splunk TLS certificates for onward forwarding and keep source secrets in the approved credential store.
Source platform requirements: Provide the source endpoint and protocol, source and destination security zones, required app/add-on, input stanza, tenant/account IDs where applicable, parsing and routing rules, expected volume, target index/sourcetype, destination group and failover behaviour.

Pattern: No add-on: HEC collector via Heavy Forwarder — Splunk Cloud
Source data: Application or integration events pushed as JSON, text, single-event or batched HEC payloads where no supported add-on exists.
Category: Custom HEC integration without vendor app/add-on
Source mechanism: Source-native HTTPS push to Splunk HEC
Collection tier / runtime: Splunk Heavy Forwarder acting as HEC collector
Transport: HTTPS to HEC; Splunk-to-Splunk over TLS
Required app / add-on: None; use platform or custom parsing configuration where required
Port / firewall requirements: Allow source systems to TCP 8088 or 443 on the Heavy Forwarder HEC listener; allow outbound TCP 9997 to <stack>.splunkcloud.com from the Heavy Forwarder; allow outbound TCP 8089 to the deployment server where the forwarder or Heavy Forwarder is centrally managed. Restrict HEC ingress to approved source networks.
Authentication requirements: Use a dedicated HEC token on the Heavy Forwarder with least-privilege index access. Validate TLS and use client certificates/mutual TLS where required. Splunk forwarding uses the configured TLS trust to the final destination.
Source platform requirements: Provide the Heavy Forwarder HEC endpoint, token reference, event/raw endpoint, source IP allowlist, payload schema, timestamp, index, sourcetype, source and host metadata, batching limits, indexer acknowledgement setting and expected event volume.

Pattern: Direct HEC to Splunk Cloud

Source mechanism: Source-native HTTPS push to Splunk Cloud HEC
Port / firewall requirements: Allow source systems outbound TCP 443 to https://<stack>.splunkcloud.com:443/services/collector or the stack-specific HEC hostname. Permit DNS resolution and TLS certificate validation, and restrict egress to the approved Splunk Cloud endpoint.
Authentication requirements: Use a dedicated Splunk Cloud HEC token with the minimum required index access. Validate the Splunk Cloud certificate; use a source-side secret store and rotate/revoke the token through the governed process.
Source platform requirements: Provide the Splunk Cloud stack/HEC FQDN, token reference, event or raw endpoint, index, sourcetype, source and host metadata, payload schema, timestamp format, batching and retry behaviour, and indexer acknowledgement setting where supported.

Pattern: REST API polling via Azure Function → Splunk Cloud HEC
Source data: Vendor REST API records such as audit, alert, activity, inventory, configuration and operational telemetry collected by custom code.
Category: Custom REST API polling script to HEC
Transport: HTTPS to source REST API; HTTPS to HEC
Required app / add-on: None; custom script and platform parsing configuration
Port / firewall requirements: Allow outbound TCP 443 from the runtime to the source REST API and allow TCP 443 to the Splunk Cloud HEC endpoint. Permit DNS, TLS certificate validation and identity/secret-service endpoints. Where VNet integration is used, add the required NSG, route, NAT, proxy or private-endpoint rules for both the source API and HEC.
Authentication requirements: Configure the source API credential required by the vendor, such as OAuth 2.0 client credentials, API key, bearer token, certificate or service username/password, plus a dedicated least-privilege HEC token for delivery. Pattern: Syslog server with forwarder collection — Splunk Cloud
Source data: Network and security appliance syslog written by rsyslog or syslog-ng to controlled files, including firewall, router, switch, VPN, proxy, load balancer and infrastructure events.
Category: Syslog server with forwarder file collection
Direction: Push to syslog server; forwarder monitors written files
Source mechanism: Source sends syslog to a syslog server
Collection tier / runtime: Syslog server plus Splunk Universal Forwarder or Heavy Forwarder
Transport: UDP, TCP or TLS syslog; Splunk-to-Splunk over TLS
Required app / add-on: Vendor TA or custom parsing where available; generic syslog otherwise
Port / firewall requirements: Allow source devices to the syslog server on UDP/TCP 514 or TCP 6514 for TLS; allow outbound TCP 9997 to <stack>.splunkcloud.com from the Universal or Heavy Forwarder; allow outbound TCP 8089 to the deployment server where the forwarder or Heavy Forwarder is centrally managed. Restrict listeners to approved source networks.
Authentication requirements: UDP/TCP syslog normally has no application credential. Use server certificates and optional mutual TLS for TLS syslog. The forwarder service account requires read access to the written files, and Splunk forwarding uses the configured TLS certificate or mutual-TLS trust.
Source platform requirements: Provide each source hostname/IP, vendor/product, target syslog server, protocol/port, facility/severity and message format. Define syslog listener rules, output file paths, ownership/permissions, rotation/retention/compression, forwarder monitor stanzas, host metadata, index, sourcetype and expected EPS.
